translations.literal: Wang Lantian and Liu Anxi were both eminent and weighty and at first did not decline—how can one now admire this non-declining?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lantian and Liu Anxi were both eminent and at first did not decline—how can we now imitate their refusal to decline?

sentences.zh: 孫興公、孔顗竝讓記室，今豈可三署皆讓邪？

translations.literal: Sun Xinggong and Kong Yan both declined the recorder's post—how can one now decline all three offices?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xinggong and Kong Yan both declined the recorder's post—how can one decline all three offices now?

sentences.zh: 謝吏部今授超階，讓別有意，豈關官之大小？

translations.literal: Xie of the Ministry of Personnel now receives a rank beyond his step—his declining has a separate intent; how does it concern the office's size?
translations.idiomatic: Xie of the Ministry is now promoted beyond his rank—his declining has its own meaning; what has that to do with the size of the office?

sentences.zh: 撝讓之美，本出人情。

translations.literal: The beauty of yielding and declining springs from human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of yielding springs from human feeling.

sentences.zh: 若大官必讓，便與詣闕章表不異。

translations.literal: If great offices must decline, it is no different from presenting a memorial at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: If high offices must always decline, it is no different from a formal memorial at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 例旣如此，謂都自非疑。

translations.literal: Since precedent is thus, I say altogether there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Since the precedents are clear, I see no doubt at all.

sentences.zh: 」朓又啓讓，上優答不許。

translations.literal: " Tiao again memorialized to decline; the Emperor graciously replied and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Tiao memorialized again to decline; the emperor graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 朓善草隷，長五言詩，沈約常云「二百年來無此詩也」。

translations.literal: Tiao was skilled in cursive and clerical script and excelled at five-word poetry; Shen Yue often said, "In two hundred years there has been no poetry like this."
translations.idiomatic: Tiao was skilled in cursive and clerical script and excelled at five-character verse; Shen Yue often said, "In two hundred years there has been no poetry like this."

sentences.zh: 敬皇后遷祔山陵，朓撰哀策文，齊世莫有及者。

translations.literal: When the Respectful Empress was moved to join the imperial tomb, Tiao composed the lamentation text; in the Qi age none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Respectful Empress was moved to the imperial tomb, Tiao composed the lamentation text, unmatched in the Qi age.

sentences.zh: 東昏失德，江祐欲立夏王寶玄，末更回惑，與弟祀密謂朓曰：「江夏年少輕脫，不堪負荷神器，不可復行廢立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang You wished to establish the Prince of Xia, Bao Xuan, but at the end wavered again; with his brother Si he secretly told Tiao: "The Prince of Jiangxia is young, frivolous, and light—he cannot bear the regalia of the divine vessel; we cannot again carry out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang You wished to make the Prince of Xia, Bao Xuan, emperor, but later wavered; he and his brother Si secretly told Tiao, "The Prince of Jiangxia is young and frivolous and cannot bear the throne; we cannot depose and establish again.

sentences.zh: 始安年長入纂，不乖物望。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shi'an is older in entering succession and does not go against popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shi'an is older and would succeed without going against popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 非以此要富貴，政是求安國家耳。

translations.literal: It is not by this to seek wealth and honor—it is truly to seek the state's peace.
translations.idiomatic: We do not seek wealth and honor by this—we seek only the state's peace.

sentences.zh: 」遙光又遣親人劉渢密致意於朓，欲以爲肺腑。

translations.literal: " Yaoguang also sent his close man Liu Hong to convey intentions secretly to Tiao, wishing to make him a heart-and-belly confidant.
translations.idiomatic: " Yaoguang also sent his confidant Liu Hong to convey his intentions secretly to Tiao, wishing to make him an intimate ally.

sentences.zh: 朓自以受恩高宗，非渢所言，不肯答。

translations.literal: Tiao himself thought he had received favor from the High Ancestor and that Hong's words were not acceptable; he refused to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao considered that he owed his favor to the High Ancestor and would not accept what Hong said; he refused to reply.

sentences.zh: 少日，遙光以朓兼知衞尉事，朓懼見引，卽以祏等謀告左興盛，興盛不敢發言。

translations.literal: A few days later Yaoguang had Tiao additionally manage Court of the Imperial Clan affairs; Tiao feared being drawn in and at once reported Si and the others' plot to Zuo Xingsheng, who did not dare speak out.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Yaoguang had Tiao additionally manage Court of the Imperial Clan affairs; fearing entanglement, Tiao reported Si's plot to Zuo Xingsheng, who did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 祏聞，以告遙光，遙光大怒，乃稱敕召朓，仍回車付廷尉，與徐孝嗣、祏、暄等連名啓誅朓曰：「謝朓資性險薄，大彰遠近。

translations.literal: Si heard and told Yaoguang; Yaoguang was greatly enraged, then in the emperor's name summoned Tiao, turned the carriage back and handed him to the Minister of Justice; with Xu Xiaosi, Si, Xuan, and others he jointly memorialized to execute Tiao, saying: "Xie Tiao's nature is dangerous and thin, greatly manifest near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Si heard and told Yaoguang, who was furious; summoning Tiao in the emperor's name, he turned him over to the Minister of Justice; with Xu Xiaosi, Si, Xuan, and others he jointly memorialized for Tiao's execution: "Xie Tiao's nature is treacherous and shallow, notorious far and near.

sentences.zh: 王敬則往構凶逆，微有誠效，自爾昇擢，超越倫伍。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze formerly plotted treason; he had slight sincere effect, and from then was promoted beyond his rank and peers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze had plotted treason; Tiao's small service in exposing it won promotion beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 而谿壑無厭，著於觸事。

translations.literal: Yet ravines and gullies know no satiety, manifest in whatever he touches.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his greed knew no limit, shown in everything he did.

sentences.zh: 比遂扇動內外，處處姦說，妄貶乘輿，竊論宮禁，閒謗親賢，輕議朝宰，醜言異計，非可具聞。

translations.literal: Recently he has stirred inside and outside, everywhere treacherous speech, recklessly demeaning the imperial carriage, privately discussing palace prohibitions, idly slandering kin and worthies, lightly debating court ministers—ugly words and strange schemes not to be fully heard.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he has stirred court and country, spreading treacherous talk everywhere, demeaning the throne, discussing palace secrets, slandering kin and worthies, and lightly attacking ministers—ugly words and strange schemes too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 無君之心旣著，共棄之誅宜及。

translations.literal: His heart without a ruler is already manifest; the punishment of collective rejection should reach him.
translations.idiomatic: His disloyal heart is already plain; the punishment of collective rejection should fall on him.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜下北里，肅正刑書。

translations.literal: Your subjects jointly deliberate: he should be sent to North Lane and the penal code solemnly applied.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly recommend that he be sent to prison and the penal code solemnly applied.

sentences.zh: 」詔：「公等啓事如此，朓資性輕險，久彰物議。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Your report is thus; Tiao's nature is light and dangerous, long manifest in public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict read: "Your report is as stated; Tiao's nature is frivolous and dangerous and has long been notorious.

sentences.zh: 直以彫蟲薄伎，見齒衣冠。

translations.literal: Merely because of carving-insect petty skill he was counted among caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was admitted to the ranks of officials only for his petty literary skill.

sentences.zh: 昔在渚宮，構扇蕃邸，日夜縱諛，仰窺俯畫。

translations.literal: Formerly at the Isle Palace he plotted and fanned the prince's mansion, day and night indulging flattery, looking up to spy and looking down to scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at the Isle Palace he stirred up the prince's household, flattering day and night, spying above and plotting below.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，飜自宣露，江、漢無波，以爲己功。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he turned and exposed it himself—the Yangzi and Han without waves he took as his own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital he boasted of it himself, claiming credit though the Yangzi and Han were calm.

sentences.zh: 素論於茲而盡，縉紳所以側目。

translations.literal: Plain discussion ended here; that is why the girdled and sashed turned their eyes sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion ended there, which is why officials looked askance at him.

sentences.zh: 去夏之事，頗有微誠，賞擢曲加，踰邁倫序，感悅未聞，陵競彌著。

translations.literal: Last summer's affair had some slight sincerity; reward and promotion were bent to add beyond rank and order—gratitude and joy were not heard, overbearing rivalry grew all the more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Last summer's affair showed some small loyalty, and reward was bent to promote him beyond his rank—yet no gratitude was heard, and his arrogance grew only worse.

sentences.zh: 遂復矯構風塵，妄惑朱紫，詆貶朝政，疑閒親賢。

translations.literal: Then again he falsely constructed wind and dust, recklessly confusing purple and red, slandering court governance, sowing doubt and estranging kin and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Then again he stirred up trouble, confusing high and low office, slandering the government and sowing doubt among kin and worthies.

sentences.zh: 巧言利口，見醜前志，涓流纖孽，作戒遠圖。

translations.literal: Clever words and sharp tongue are seen as ugly in former records; trickling streams and slender evils make warnings for far-reaching plans.
translations.idiomatic: Clever words and sharp tongue are condemned in the histories; small streams of evil make warnings for far-reaching plans.

sentences.zh: 宜有少正之刑，以申去害之義。

translations.literal: He should receive the punishment of Shaozheng, to declare the meaning of removing harm.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive the punishment of Shaozheng, to declare the meaning of removing harm.

sentences.zh: 便可收付廷尉，肅明國典。

translations.literal: He may at once be taken and handed to the Minister of Justice, solemnly clarifying the state code.
translations.idiomatic: Take him at once to the Minister of Justice and solemnly apply the state code.

sentences.zh: 」又使御史中丞范岫奏收朓，下獄死。

translations.literal: " He also had Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialize to arrest Tiao; he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He also had Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialize to arrest Tiao; he was imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 朓初告王敬則，敬則女爲朓妻，常懷刀欲報朓，朓不敢相見。

translations.literal: When Tiao first reported Wang Jingze, Jingze's daughter was Tiao's wife and constantly carried a knife wishing to avenge Tiao; Tiao did not dare meet her.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiao first reported Wang Jingze, Jingze's daughter was Tiao's wife and often carried a knife to avenge her father; Tiao did not dare meet her.

sentences.zh: 及爲吏部郎，沈昭略謂朓曰：「卿人地之美，無忝此職。

translations.literal: When he became Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel, Shen Zhaolue said to Tiao: "Your person and place are beautiful—you do not disgrace this office.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel, Shen Zhaolue said to him, "Your birth and talent do not disgrace this office.

sentences.zh: 但恨今日刑于寡妻。

translations.literal: I only regret that today you suffer punishment from a widowed wife."
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that today you suffer at the hands of a widowed wife."

sentences.zh: 」朓臨敗歎曰：「我不殺王公，王公由我而死。」

translations.literal: " Facing defeat Tiao sighed: "I did not kill the prince, but the prince died because of me."
translations.idiomatic: " Facing ruin Tiao sighed, "I did not kill the prince, but the prince died because of me."

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: Commentary and Praise
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Commentary and Praise

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉世遷宅江表，人無北歸之計，英霸作輔，芟定中原，彌見金德之不競也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In the Jin age they moved their residence south of the Yangzi; men had no plan to return north. When heroic hegemons served as assistants and mowed down the Central Plains, it only showed all the more that the Jin virtue could not compete.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: In the Jin age the court moved south of the Yangzi and men abandoned any plan to return north; when heroic ministers briefly reconquered the Central Plains, it only showed how far the Jin mandate had fallen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉再略河南，師旅傾覆，自此以來，攻伐寢議。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia they again seized Henan, but armies overturned and collapsed; from then on, campaigns and attacks ceased from discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia they again seized Henan, but the armies were destroyed; since then offensive war has scarcely been debated.

sentences.zh: 雖有戰爭，事存保境。

translations.literal: Though there was war, the affair remained preserving the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Though war continued, the aim remained merely to hold the borders.

sentences.zh: 王融生遇永明，軍國寧息，以文敏才華，不足進取，經略心旨，殷懃表奏。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was born into Yongming, when army and state were tranquil; with literary quickness and talent insufficient for advancement by office, he put his strategic intent into earnest memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was born in the Yongming era, when army and state were at peace; his literary brilliance could not win advancement by office alone, so he poured his strategic vision into earnest memorials.

sentences.zh: 若使宮車未晏，有事邊關，融之報效，或不易限。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage had not yet grown late and there were affairs at the frontier passes, Rong's repayment of service might not have been easy to limit.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor had not died young and trouble had arisen at the frontier, Rong's service might have been hard to limit.

sentences.zh: 夫經國體遠，許久爲難，而立功立事，信居物右，其賈誼終軍之流亞乎！

translations.literal: Governing the state and embodying the far—such is acknowledged as difficult; yet establishing achievement and establishing affairs truly stand to the right among things—is he not next after the stream of Jia Yi and Zhong Jun!
translations.idiomatic: To govern the state with far-reaching vision is acknowledged as difficult, yet to achieve real deeds truly stands above common things—is he not of the company of Jia Yi and Zhong Jun!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元長穎脫，拊翼將飛。

translations.literal: The praise says: Yuanchang was sharp and outstanding, beating wings about to fly.
translations.idiomatic: The praise says: Yuanchang was brilliant and ready, beating his wings to fly.

sentences.zh: 時來運往，身沒志違。

translations.literal: The time came and fortune passed; the body perished and the will was thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: The time came and fortune passed; he died and his will was thwarted.

sentences.zh: 高宗始業，乃顧玄暉。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor began his enterprise, he then turned to Xuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor began his enterprise, he turned to Xuanhui.

sentences.zh: 逢昏屬亂，先蹈禍機。

translations.literal: Meeting a benighted age belonging to chaos, he first trod the mechanism of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting a benighted age and chaotic times, he was first to tread the path of disaster.

translations.idiomatic: Section divider.

translations.literal: Note
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note
